subject: Post-demo: sample corpus intake & quality flags for generative QA pilot

Subject: Post-demo: sample corpus intake & quality flags for generative QA pilot

Hi Elena / Tom —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and concrete asks so we can scope the pilot and the evals team can start preparing: 

Summary of what we heard
- Use case: generative QA over internal SOPs + ticket text (short to medium context length, lots of domain acronyms).
- Target SLAs: 99th pct token latency < 600ms for per-turn generation; acceptable throughput ~20 qps for the pilot.
- Data sensitivity: mix of PII (names, emails) and moderately sensitive health-adjacent notes.

Redwood recommendations (high-level)
- Start with a 13B instruction-tuned open model; keep a smaller 7B as fallback for bursty traffic.
- Use prefix caching for repeated SOP queries, and an initial KV cache TTL of 10m for session continuity.

Asks / next steps (please):
1) Share a representative prompt sample set (10–50 queries) showing typical phrasing + edge cases (abbreviated records, misspellings, truncated ticket threads). If you can, upload a CSV — column headers: query, context_snippet, redaction_required (yes/no).
2) Highlight the top 3 categories you consider "sensitive" for redaction (e.g., patient_name, account_id, contract_terms).
3) Confirm timeline: can you share the CSV by EOD next Wednesday (Jun 21)?

I've attached a short pilot_scope.xlsx with suggested acceptance criteria and an initial eval checklist. Ben and Aditya are CC'd for model/benchmark questions.

Attachments: pilot_scope.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

Thanks —
Kimberly Park
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com

From: Elena Rivera <elena.rivera@medisolve.com>

Date: Fri, 14 Jun 2028 16:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: sample corpus intake & quality flags for generative QA pilot

Thanks Kimberly — good recap. A few clarifications and a quick data note:

1) Redaction: our data team can mark patient_name and account_id as "always redacted". For other fields like case_notes we prefer guidance rather than automatic removal.
2) Sample size: we can export a CSV with ~300 rows by next Tuesday (Jun 19). The CSV will be sanitized but will keep realistic truncation and misspellings. Will include a boolean column for redaction_required.
3) Edge cases: we have many short logs that are just 1–2 words (e.g., "escalated", "left voicemail") — these seem to cause hallucinations in other models. Please flag how you want those represented.

Attached a tiny inline sample below (we'll upload the CSV formally):

query,context_snippet,redaction_required
"How do I reset patient portal access?","Patient: *redacted*; ticket: reset link expired",yes
"Billing code for procedure X","Code: 99213 (billing note truncated)",no
"What does "escalated" mean on KBA?","escalated — see notes",no

Also: can you share benchmarking expectations so we can compare with our in-house test harness?

Thanks,
Elena Rivera
Head of Product
MediSolve
elena.rivera@medisolve.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Jun 2028 08:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: sample corpus intake & quality flags for generative QA pilot

Kimberly / Aditya —

Quick technical notes to add before we ingest customer samples: 

Model & perf recommendations:
- Start evaluation on a Mistral-style 13B instruction-tuned model (quantized to 4-bit if using dedicated infra) for cost/perf balance. Baseline expected median latency: ~180–250ms single-token on A100-like; 99th depends on batching and KV cache hit rate.
- Keep a distilled 7B as an overflow variant for cost isolation during peak periods.

Quality / regression flags to include in the eval harness:
- Hallucination rate measured by exact-match and entailment-based scoring on a labeled subset (we recommend a 200-row labeled ground truth set).
- Short-context hallucination: track failure rate on queries with context_snippet length < 40 chars — these are often problematic.
- Redaction leakage: after automated redaction, measure any tokens that contain PII-like patterns using regex detectors.

Benchmarks & assets:
- I've uploaded an internal snapshot of our QA microbenchmarks to the shared drive (link in metadata). I'll attach a short PDF summary here for your review.

Attachment: benchmark-results-qa.pdf (summary)

If MediSolve can prioritize the short-context and redaction-required rows in the CSV, we can run targeted regressions and return a prioritized list of failure cases.

Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com

Thanks Ben — and thanks Elena for the sample preview. Short internal plan and owners: 

1) Data intake (Owner: MediSolve / Elena) — deliver CSV (ideally 200–500 rows) with redaction_required flag by Tue, Jun 19. If they can include a small labeled ground truth subset (~200 rows) that would accelerate the first eval.
2) Eval & benchmarks (Owner: Ben) — run baseline on 13B + fallback 7B, produce top-10 failure cases focusing on short-context and redaction leakage. Deliver by Fri, Jun 23.
3) Infra & perf plan (Owner: Aditya) — provide configuration recommendations (batching, cache TTLs, quant profile) and an initial cost estimate for the pilot by Mon, Jun 26.

External deliverable: we'll provide a one-page readout and a short failure-case artifact set to share with MediSolve after the first run. HubSpot deal updated: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/1234567/RDW-2028-084
